title: The wire: machines types
description: Part of the source of every type on the wire (#1135, #5380): one file per domain in Packages/Wire/schema. A $ref to another file names it (core.schema.json#/definitions/JSONValue); scripts/wire.sh gen reads them all.

AgentMachines.description: machines/forAgent: what list_machines shows an agent.

hosts.description: Every machine of the person's, by name, where start_session can start a session (#2887). Absent from an older control plane.

reason.description: Why it failed, on a make that failed (#4706).

AnnounceReply.description: What devices/announce answers: the device's record.

wait.description: Answer once the backup is made, not at once: a provider's delete waits for it (#1815).

target.description: Where backups go (#1815): this machine's folder, or the control plane's store. Left out is the machine's default: the store for a server linked to a control plane, else the folder.

canUseControl.description: The machine is linked to a control plane, so it can back up to the control plane's store (#1815).

sameDisk.description: The backup folder is on the disk of what it backs up, and not a synced folder (#2139): a backup there undoes a mistake, but is lost with the disk.

BackupStoreCommit.description: A host's backup whose parts are all uploaded: the control plane writes its .json last, then keeps the newest keep of this host's (#1815).

BackupStorePart.description: One part of a backup, at most 8 MiB (#1815): a host's upload, or the control plane's answer to a download.

name.description: On an upload, the backup's name; this host's own folder is the control plane's to say.

BranchFromRequest.description: agents/branchFrom (#1658): a new session that goes on from just before the person's prompt `entryID` in `agentID`.

BringBack.description: What folders/bringBack did (#1473): the branches that moved forward or were made, and whether the uncommitted changes were applied.

BringBackFromRequest.description: folders/bringBackFrom (#4640): Bring Back from ‹machine›… from a client. This host brings `branches` of the repository at `source` on `machine` (the control plane's id or name for it; `machineName` is the name the person knows it by, for the words), less the commits it has, and with `includeChanges` the uncommitted changes there, into the repository at `folder` here, through the control plane, as bring_back does (#2947). Branches move forward only.

BringBackNotification.description: bringBack/changed (#4640): how a bring-back that folders/bringBackFrom started goes. `read` of `total` bytes are here (0 of 0 while the bundle is made there); `finished` once it ended, whichever way: `result` is what it did, or `problem` says why it stopped, in the person's words.

BringBackRequest.description: Brings a host's branches back into this Mac's repository at `folder` (Bring back from ‹host›…, #1473): fetches the `bundle` upload, moves `branches` forward only, also where a worktree has one checked out, and applies the `patch` upload (the host's uncommitted changes) in `folder`, whose checked-out branch must be `patchOn`. It stops, and changes nothing, when a branch here has commits of its own or a worktree with a branch that moves has uncommitted changes.

BringBackSummary.description: One bring-back folders/bringBackFrom started (#4640): the folder here, and the folder on the machine it comes from.

CapacityLevel.description: A machine's capacity (#4578): ok; near (load per core above 1.5, or memory pressure warn); or full (load per core above 2.5, memory pressure critical, or swap more than half used). It rises at once, and falls only after two looks under its line.

CapacityState.description: capacity/state and capacity/changed (#4748): the machine's level, pushed when it moves, so a machine's row says it with no page open.

words.description: The level as a sentence's subject and verb: "this Mac is near capacity" or "this Mac is at capacity". Absent at ok.

CatchUpPart.description: A part this host does not know is left out of CatchUpRequest.parts.

ClientKind.description: ClientRecord.Kind: a kind a later build added reads as `unknown`.

ClientPairingRequest.description: clients/startPairing: `browser` for the web remote's code (071); a grant an older window sends is not read.

ClientRecord.description: A paired screen, as clients/list says it (ClientRecord).

DetectedServer.description: One host in the ssh config, and what machines/detect did with it (#429).

FirstBuildStartRequest.description: firstBuild/start (#5056, spec 5048 section 7): the newcomer's idea, as typed, the starter the plan page shows, and the runtime its first task set up. The host makes the folder ~/.agents/first-build when it is not there, writes the first prompt itself, so every client sends the same, and labels the session first-build. It answers with the session's id. While a first-build session that is not archived is there, it refuses with firstBuildRunning, with that session's id as the data, unless another is true (New App…, #5132).

idea.description: The person's words, as typed. Not empty.

runtimeID.description: The runtime that the plan page's first task set up, as agents/start takes it.

another.description: New App… (#5132): start one more first build, also while a first-build session is there. Absent or false keeps the newcomer's rule: refuse with firstBuildRunning.

FirstBuildStarter.description: The starter that a first build begins from (#5048): iphone-app is agentloops-dev/iphone-app-starter, web-service is agentloops-dev/web-service-starter, as make_app_repository names them.

FleetBoard.description: console/fleet's answer (#1804): every machine on the control plane, for an admin.

FleetMachine.description: One machine on Console ▸ Machines (#1804): its machines/list row, whose it is, and how many of its agents were running when it last listed them. Numbers only, never what the agents said.

ownerName.description: Its person's or bot's name; empty when nobody owns it.

bot.description: Whether its owner is a bot (#1761).

running.description: Its agents running when it last listed them; absent when it never has.

heardAt.description: When it last listed its agents.

MacPathRequest.description: mac/reveal, mac/open: a path on the host; app names the app to open it with.

MacTerminalRequest.description: mac/terminal: Terminal, in path if given.

MachineClient.description: A paired window a host may let in on its local socket (#1118), with the key it proves itself with.

person.description: The person the window belongs to (#994). The host lets it in only when it is the host's own user (FR-020).

MachineClients.description: machine/clients: every window paired with the control plane, which a host checks its local socket against (#1118).

user.description: The user the host belongs to (#994). With it, the host lets in only a window whose person is that user (FR-020); without it (an older control plane), every window listed.

MachineEnroll.description: machines/startEnroll (#1761): with as, a bot's machine code, an admin's only. Without, the caller's own, as before.

MachineFolderSend.description: machines/sendFolder, through machine/machines: one step of an agent's start_session with send (#2929), which sends this folder's branch to another of the person's machines first, or of its bring_back (#2947), which brings a branch back from there, or of its move_session (#3717), which moves a session there with its branch. Exactly one of state, upload, receive, facts, pack, read and moveIn; the control plane sends that machine's folders/receiveState, folders/receiveUpload, folders/receive, folders/sendFacts, folders/sendPack, folders/sendRead or agents/moveIn.

MachineFolderSent.description: What machines/sendFolder's step answered (#2929, #2947): state for state, folder for receive, facts for facts, pack for pack, read for read, none for upload.

MachineHello.description: machine/hello, on every connect of an uplink. `implementation` is `swift` or `go` (#1134).

capabilities.description: The capabilities this host has (#1748): each one whose methods it all serves, and the ones it declares. None from a host older than #1748.

MachineHelloAnswer.description: The control plane's answer to machine/hello (#4100): what it can do, so the host asks only what it answers, such as machine/accounts with machine.accounts/1. An older control plane answers {}: no list, so the host asks it nothing new.

capabilities.description: The control plane's capabilities (#1748), as control/status says them to a client.

MachineInfo.description: One workspace, as its provider last listed it. `state` is running, starting, stopping, stopped or unknown; or failed, for a make that failed, with the provider's `reason` (#3972). `joining` while New Machine waits for it to join the control plane, and `notJoined` once the control plane gave up waiting (#4610).

hostKeyRenews.description: Its ssh host key is made again at each start, as a Google Cloud workstation's is (#1701): after a Start the control plane made, the first ssh takes the key it is offered and pins it again.

idleTimeoutMinutes.description: The provider stops it by itself after this many minutes with no use, as GitHub stops a codespace (#4803): the machine's page says so.

reason.description: Why the make failed, in the provider's words, when `state` is failed.

joining.description: New Machine made it and the control plane waits for it to join: the row says Making… (#4610).

notJoined.description: Why the control plane gave up waiting for it to join, once it did (#4610): the row says so, with Delete.

MachineInstall.description: machines/install (MachineInstall.Request): a server over ssh, with its key, the fingerprint trusted, a tunnel. Add as Machine… names the provider and the workspace too (#3497): a codespace whose provider a machine carries is installed from that machine, with the token kept there.

MachineLink.description: machines/link. A machine whose ssh host key the control plane has not trusted yet (one that joined with the command, #3379) is refused -32069 hostKeyToTrust, data {fingerprint}, until trust is that fingerprint: the key is then kept for the machine's ssh start.

MachineProjects.description: projects/joined's answer and machine/projects (#2669): the projects that this machine's folders name, with their slots, all of them each time.

MachineProviderDraftCall.description: machine/providerDraft: a writing agent called one of the writer's tools (#858).

MachineRelease.description: machine/release (#2178): the release the control plane names, as X.Y.Z.

MachineSessionCall.description: machines/sessionCall, through machine/machines (#2927): an agent's read_session, message_session, stop_session, archive_session, or list_sessions and agent.ended wait status, on a session it started on another of the person's machines with start_session. The control plane sends that machine's agents/fromStarter, with call.from in its own words.

MachineSessionStart.description: machines/startSession, through machine/machines (#2887): an agent's start_session on another of the person's machines, by its name. The control plane sends that machine's agents/start.

MachineStatus.description: machine/status on channel 0 (#691 US4): each agent working or waiting on a person, and the next scheduled workflow.

MachineSummaryFacts.description: One of the person's other machines in machines/summaryFacts (#3354): its facts, or, when it is off or did not answer, unreached, the words that say why.

MachineUpdate.description: machines/update (#1766): a host the control plane installed over ssh, updated the same way. The server and its key are given again, as at the install, because the control plane keeps neither; the host's own root and membership stay.

MachinesSummaryFacts.description: machines/summaryFacts (#3354): the daily summary's facts from each of the person's other machines, by name.

MemoryPressure.description: The kernel's memory pressure (#4578): macOS kern.memorystatus_vm_pressure_level, or Linux PSI memory (warn when some avg10 is 10% or more, critical when full avg10 is 10% or more).

MoveAnswer.description: What a person's move came to. The message is what the window may show.

MoveNotification.description: move/changed (#4641): how a move to another machine goes, whoever asked for it. `sent` of `total` bytes of the branch are on that machine (0 of 0 while the bundle is made); `branchSent` once they are all there and the session itself goes; `finished` once it ended, whichever way: with no `problem` the session is there and gone from here, else `problem` says why it stopped, in the person's words, and the session stays here.

MoveRequest.description: The person moving an agent (053). No target takes back the person's move that is waiting.

MoveToMachineAnswer.description: What agents/moveToMachine did (#3790): the folder on that machine the session now goes on in, and whether it carries on there at once, as it was working when it moved.

MoveToMachineRequest.description: The person moving a session to another of their machines (#3790), as move_session does (#3717). `machine` is the control plane's id or name for it, and `machineName` the name the person knows it by, for the words; `folder` is an absolute path there, or, when left out, the folder of the session's project there.

PlaneMoveAction.description: What a client asks of a move of the control plane (#4255), as the Mac window's sheets do it: status says how it stands; move and return open Move to Another Machine… and Run It Here Again…; the rest are the sheets' buttons and the overview's.

PlaneMoveAsk.description: control/planeMove and control/planeMoveWanted (#4255): a client asks the window on the Mac that moves the control plane to do one step. The window does it with this Mac's control key, which never leaves the Mac.

address.description: With check on a move: where the other machine's control plane is, its https address; with no scheme, https.

PlaneMoveFlow.description: Where a move a client asked for is, as the Mac window's sheet would draw it (#4255), in its words.

kind.description: Move to Another Machine… or Run It Here Again….

step.description: The sheet's frame: key and check (P, Q or V), told (R or W), moving (S or X).

address.description: Where the control plane goes, or comes back from.

lines.description: The checks (key, check) or the stages (moving), in order.

members.description: Who has heard where it goes (told).

otherKey.description: Run It Here Again…: the other machine holds another key, so this Mac takes it first (Use Key…).

checked.description: Every check passed: Tell Everyone may be asked.

busy.description: A check or a step runs on the Mac now.

taken.description: The other end serves now: Cancel can't undo it.

failed.description: A stage failed: Close, not Cancel.

PlaneMoveLine.description: One check or stage of a move (#4255).

note.description: Why it failed, or a note under it.

PlaneMoveMember.description: A window, phone or machine of the control plane, and whether it knows where the control plane goes (#4255).

kind.description: What it is, and when it last connected, in words.

PlaneMoveRow.description: A row of the control plane's move card (#4255): Move to Another Machine, This Mac moved its control plane, a forwarding row, or the way back's.

confirm.description: Asked before the action, as Stop forwarding?'s message.

ProcessesState.description: processes/list (#3453): the machine's totals and the daemon's process tree, in tree order, the daemon first. At most 200 processes; omitted counts the rest.

ProjectMachine.description: A machine of projects/sessions (#3276) that has a folder of the project, by id and name.

ProjectMachineFolders.description: One machine of machines/projectFolders (#3277): its id and name, and the absolute paths of its folders in the project.

ProviderAdd.description: providers/add and providers/update. `machine` is the machine that carries the provider (#3398): it runs the provider's server, and `secrets` go on to it, never kept by the control plane. None picks the caller's first online machine; an update without it keeps the one it has. `cli` is not kept; `draft` is the draft this accepts (#858).

ProviderCarried.description: What a provider's machine answers to providers/carry, providers/keepSecrets, providers/forget and providers/ssh (#3398): the call's result, or why it failed, in words for the person. Channel 0 has no error path.

ProviderCarry.description: providers/carry (#3398): the control plane asks the machine that carries a provider to call it. `record` is the provider's record, which never holds a secret; the machine runs its server with the secrets it keeps. `secrets` is only a draft's, for this call, and is not kept.

ProviderCreate.description: providers/create. With no `id`, the person's default provider: the first one added that they may make machines from (#3972). With no `name`, `machine-N`, from the person's own counter. With no `options`, the provider's defaults: each field's `default`, or else the first of its `enum`.

repository.description: The repository to start it from (#1809), an https git address. A provider whose New Machine form has `repository`, such as Codespaces, makes the workspace from it; any other has the host clone it once it joins, before `clones`.

ProviderDraftAnswer.description: providers/draftAnswer: yes or no to a question.

ProviderDraftAnswered.description: A draft answered with no agent: the server follows the contract, or a shipped map fits.

ProviderDraftSign.description: The writing agent's start, for the client that asked for the draft to sign (#3542): the machine that holds its person's lock takes no start the control plane sends in its own words. The client checks that it starts only a draft's writer (agents/start, the draft's purpose, sandboxed, no MCP servers or other folders), signs method and params as they are (a LockSignature to machine), and sends the signature with providers/draftSigned.

ProviderDraftSigned.description: providers/draftSigned (#3542): the signature of a draft's sign, which the control plane delivers with the start as it came.

ProviderDraftUpdate.description: control/providerDraft: how a draft stands, to the client that started it.

ProviderOptions.description: providers/options: the New Machine form, a JSON Schema, with what New Machine would make (#4634). With no `id`, the person's default provider.

id.description: The provider the form is for: the one asked for, or else the person's default.

values.description: The values the form starts with: the options the person made a machine with last on this provider, over each field's `default` or else the first of its `enum`.

name.description: The name New Machine would give: the person's next `machine-N`. Not kept until a make uses it.

ProviderRequest.description: providers/remove, providers/refresh, providers/options (with no `id`, the default provider).

ProviderRuntimes.description: providers/runtimes: what may write, on which host, or why none.

ProviderSSH.description: providers/ssh (#3398): the machine that carries a codespaces provider starts a codespace's agentsd over ssh (`start`), reads its host key (`hostKey`), installs Agents in it with a host code from the control plane (`install`, #3497), or holds an ssh session to it that GitHub counts as use while its machine works (`keepAwake`, renewed each few minutes, and `letSleep`, #4637), with the token it keeps. Its result is ProviderSSHResult.

hostCode.description: install's host code: the codespace runs the control plane's install.sh with it, from the address and pin it names.

ProviderSSHResult.description: providers/ssh's result (#3398): the host key taken, in known_hosts form, and for hostKey a fingerprint to trust first.

ProviderSummary.description: A provider for the Providers page, never its commands, headers or secrets' values.

group.description: The group whose users may use it (#1761); none is the admins' alone.

mayUse.description: The caller may start machines from it (#1761): they are in its group. Absent from an older control plane, which lets everyone.

default.description: New Machine makes the caller's machines on it (#3979): the one they made a machine on last or chose with Make Default, or else the first one added. True on one provider at most; absent from an older control plane.

machine.description: The machine that carries it: runs its server and keeps its secrets (#3398). Absent for one made before, which must be added again.

machineOffline.description: Its machine is offline: its machines can't be started, stopped, made or deleted until it is back (#3398).

sshToolMissing.description: The CLI its machines are reached through over ssh (gh, coder) when the control plane's machine has none (#3367). Absent when it needs none or has it.

ReceiveRequest.description: Makes or brings up to date a host's copy of a Mac's repository (#1123): fetches the `bundle` upload, moves `branches` forward only, checks out `checkout`, sets `origin`, applies the `patch` upload (uncommitted changes), and adds the folder as a folder. It stops, and changes nothing, when the host has changes or commits of its own.

ReceiveState.description: What a host has at a folder before a send (#1123). `heads` are the commits of its branches, so the Mac's bundle carries only what the host lacks. `ownChanges` is true when the folder has changes that the last send did not put there.

ReceiveStateRequest.description: Asks a host about a folder a Mac will send a repository to (Send to ‹host›…, #1123). `folder` may start with ~/.

ReceiveUploadRequest.description: One part of a file a Mac sends (#1123), at `offset` in the upload. A part is at most 16 MB; the host keeps the upload until folders/receive uses it.

RequiredCapabilities.description: What the control plane needs of a peer to route for it (#1748): a host without each of host is needsUpdate, and a client without each of client is answered -32008.

accountFolderVariable.description: The variable that names the folder its sign-in is kept in, for a runtime that can have more than one account (#840): CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, CODEX_HOME.

setBy.description: Set when the organisation's policy does not allow this runtime here (#998, FR-010).

version.description: The installed copy's version: the toolset's pinned version for the app's own copy, else what the runtime's --version says (#3674). Absent when it is not installed or does not say.

SSHHost.description: A server ssh knows by a name, for Add a Machine's server box (#610).

SSHHostsRequest.description: machines/sshHosts (#610): with a destination, just that, as typed.

SelfUpdate.description: How a Mac's host updates Agents Host to the release the control plane names, with no administrator (#2178).

release.description: The release the control plane named last; none until it names one.

message.description: Why it failed or cannot, in a sentence for the person.

SelfUpdateState.description: Where updating Agents Host is (#2178): upToDate, off (the person turned it off), downloading, waiting (ready; it waits for the last turn to end), restarting, failed (the next release named tries again), cannot (this copy cannot update itself, such as one in a folder only an administrator changes).

SendFacts.description: What the Send sheet shows (#1123): the local branches, the one checked out (none when detached), the origin, and whether anything is uncommitted.

SendFactsRequest.description: Asks this Mac's host about a repository to send (Send to ‹host›…, #1123).

SendFile.description: A file the host made for a send, read with folders/sendRead (#1123).

SendNotification.description: send/changed (#4613): how a send that folders/send started goes. `sent` of `total` bytes are on the other machine (0 of 0 while the bundle is made); `finished` once it ended, whichever way: `received` is the folder it became there, or `problem` says why it stopped, in the person's words.

SendPack.description: What folders/sendPack made (#1123): each branch at its commit, the bundle (none when the receiving host has every commit) and the patch (none when nothing is uncommitted).

SendPackRequest.description: Makes what a send carries (#1123): a bundle of `branches` without the commits in `leavingOut` (the receiving host's), and with `includeChanges` a patch of the uncommitted changes, new files git does not ignore among them.

SendRead.description: A part of at most 1 MB (#1530). `end` is true for the last, and then the host removes the file.

SendReadRequest.description: One part of a file folders/sendPack made, from `offset` (#1123).

SendRequest.description: folders/send (#4613): Send to ‹machine›… from a client. This host sends `branches` of the repository at `folder`, less the commits the folder there has, and with `includeChanges` its uncommitted changes, to `destination` on `machine` (the control plane's id or name for it; `machineName` is the name the person knows it by, for the words), through the control plane, as start_session with send does (#2929). There `checkout` is checked out and `origin` set.

SendSummary.description: One send folders/send started (#4613): the folder here, and the folder on the machine it goes to.

SentBranch.description: A branch the Mac sends, at the commit it has (#1123).

SessionMoveIn.description: agents/moveIn (#3717): a session moving here from another of the person's machines, with move_session. `upload` is the export of its record and its transcript, sent with folders/receiveUpload; `folder` is the folder here it goes on in, where its branch was sent first. It keeps its id, labels and times, and goes on in this machine's root; its runtime reads the app's record ahead of its next prompt (`movedFrom`). `from` is the machine it leaves (the control plane writes `machine`), and the agent there that started it, when that agent stays there. With `carryOn`, it starts again here at once, as it was working when it moved.

SessionMovedFrom.description: The machine a session moved here from with move_session (#3717), and when.

summary.description: The command and its first arguments, or the URL without its query.

clash.description: The runtimes with a server of this name in their own config, and that file.

Simulator.description: An iOS simulator on a Mac host (#842): its UDID, its name, its system and whether it is booted.

SimulatorList.description: simulators/list: the host's simulators, booted first. Reason says why there are none to list, when a host has no simulators (not a Mac, no Xcode).

SimulatorRequest.description: simulators/boot and simulators/shutdown: one simulator, by its UDID.

SimulatorScreen.description: A booted simulator's screen as a JPEG, and its size in pixels.

SimulatorScreenRequest.description: simulators/screen: a booted simulator's screen, at most maxHeight pixels tall (1200 when left out).

SimulatorTapRequest.description: simulators/tap: a touch on a booted simulator's screen, where from 0 to 1 across (x) and down (y).

StartedMachinePreview.description: A started machine in people/removePreview: the branches and worktrees on it with work that is not pushed. `unknown` says why it could not be asked (offline, or it did not answer), and then `unpushed` is empty.

WakeSettings.description: Whether this Mac is kept awake for agents, and for how long after they stop (024), as wake.json in the root.

warmRuntimes.description: How many finished sessions keep their runtime running, ready for a reply (#183, #4044): 0 to 8, default 3, 0 turning the warm pool off. A runtime with background processes does not count against it.

backgroundHours.description: How long a finished runtime whose background processes (a dev server, a build, a watcher) still run is kept, counted from its last turn's end (#4044): 1 to 24 hours, default 4. Its processes are then ended with it. 0, or missing, from a client that does not know it, keeps the value the host has.

releaseAfterMinutes.description: How long a finished runtime with no background processes is kept, counted from its last turn's end, before the host ends it (#4044, #4513): 0 to 1440 minutes, default 10. An agent that waits for an event (wait_for_event, a lease) is then continued with session/load when the event comes. 0 releases none for being idle; warmRuntimes still holds. Missing, from a client that does not know it, keeps the value the host has. A runtime that can neither load nor resume a conversation is kept while its agent waits.

WakeState.description: Why the Mac is, or is not, being kept awake (024).

WebPagePairing.description: machine/pairWebPage (#4214): the web page's address with a one-time browser code after #code=, for the agent browser to open.

WebServe.description: control/setWeb (#4252, 071 FR-002): serve Agents to browsers on the control plane's Mac, or stop. Off closes the loopback listener; a page open through it stays connected.
